classificationDefinitions.verified-native: Primary documentation explicitly supports the raw loader location and the invocation controls used by the Forge; no transform is required and a reproducible probe is supplied.
classificationDefinitions.format-validated: The raw skill is documented as discoverable or was enumerated by the harness, but a required invocation-policy behavior is absent, removed, or not proven.
classificationDefinitions.documented-adapter: Primary documentation provides a real target surface, but a path or format transform is required; the adapter is described and is not assumed to exist.
classificationDefinitions.unsupported/unknown: No primary evidence establishes a reliable filesystem import contract for Forge skills.

probeEvidenceStatusDefinitions.unrun: No step of the stated pass-criteria probe was executed.
probeEvidenceStatusDefinitions.partial: Some relevant evidence was collected, but the full stated pass criteria were not exercised or satisfied.
probeEvidenceStatusDefinitions.passed: Every stated pass criterion was exercised and satisfied.
probeEvidenceStatusDefinitions.failed: The stated probe was exercised and at least one pass criterion was not satisfied.

invariants: No universal support claim without per-harness primary documentation and a reproducible probe.
Discovery does not prove invocation-policy equivalence.
A description-level prohibition is advisory and does not preserve explicit-only invocation.
User-only islands are omitted by default on any harness without an enforced explicit-only equivalent.
Transforms are generated in scratch output and never rewrite canonical islands in place.
Unknowns remain unknown until a current product probe or primary source closes them.

harnesses.name: claude.ai custom-skill upload

loader.path: Settings or Customize > Skills > upload ZIP

formatContract.documentedTension: The Help Center calls dependencies optional metadata, but the dedicated upload validator contract excludes dependencies from the six accepted top-level fields; this adapter does not emit it top-level.

steps: Build a scratch ZIP whose single top-level entry is the named skill folder and whose entrypoint is <skill-name>/SKILL.md; do not place skill files directly at archive root or under an extra wrapper directory.
Retain only name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, and allowed-tools as top-level frontmatter fields.
Generate and review a routing-equivalent description of at most 200 characters for each of the 48 over-limit islands; preserve capability and Use when intent.
Move extension values into namespaced metadata for provenance only.
Omit all 13 user-only islands unless the operator explicitly waives loss of enforced policy.

invocationPolicy.explicit: account UI selection is documented at product level
invocationPolicy.disableModelInvocation: cannot be represented: claude.ai hard-rejects this non-spec top-level field and metadata is inert annotation

claims: six accepted top-level fields for claude.ai uploads
hard rejection of any other top-level field
same upload rules for enabled Cowork and cloud skills

probe.command: Upload one raw extended canary and one transformed root-folder ZIP to a disposable claude.ai profile; record exact acceptance/error and invocation behavior.
probe.passCriteria: Raw extended canary reproduces the documented hard error; transformed root-folder ZIP uploads and enables; explicit and implicit behavior are separately observed.
probe.observation: A supplied earlier session observed hard rejection of the 13 extended islands. Current Anthropic documentation independently confirms the six-key allow-list and hard-error rule; this contract did not rerun a live account upload.

unknowns: Whether the documented rejection and transformed upload reproduce on the current account surface.
Current account-surface explicit-versus-implicit invocation behavior after upload.
How Anthropic intends the Help Center dependencies guidance to coexist with the six-key upload validator.
risks: Successful ZIP upload would prove format acceptance only, not explicit-only enforcement.
